title: OpenAI evaluation error triage
summary: Helps practitioners avoid recording permission and timeout failures as unsupported evidence-record failure classes. The authoritative classifications and provider-specific remediation remain UNKNOWN until the governing schema and current first-party guidance are available.
prerequisites: Access to the authoritative evidence-record specification
Access to the evaluation failure being investigated
Access to current first-party OpenAI guidance for the affected operation

sections.title: Answer first
paragraphs: Should you record permission or timeout failures as PERMISSION or TIMEOUT in the evidence-record FAILURE CLASS field? No. The inspection establishes that neither value appears in the field's enum. The correct replacement classifications are UNKNOWN, so do not substitute guessed values.

This is an intermediate-level correction. Permission handling, timeout retry eligibility, retry limits, delay behavior, and the action to take after retries fail are UNKNOWN because the authoritative evidence-record specification and applicable first-party provider guidance were not supplied.

Which of the three previously cited sources moved or passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN. Their titles, prior URLs, replacement URL, and contents were not supplied. The source-specific effect is therefore also UNKNOWN. The unsupported 2026-07-25 verification dates cannot establish that those sources were checked on that date.

sections.title: Correction procedure
paragraphs: Step 1: Obtain the authoritative evidence-record specification and inspect the complete allowed set for FAILURE CLASS. If the specification is unavailable or its HTTPS location cannot be opened, stop the classification change and request the specification from the maintainer responsible for it. Do not infer an allowed value from the failure description.

Step 2: Determine how the specification represents the observed permission or timeout condition. If no permitted representation is documented, mark the mapping UNKNOWN outside the evidence record and request a schema decision. Do not insert PERMISSION or TIMEOUT into the enum.

Step 3: Check current first-party OpenAI guidance before deciding that a timeout is transient or retryable, or before selecting remediation for a permission failure. If applicable guidance cannot be opened or does not address the condition, leave the retry or remediation claim UNKNOWN and escalate the case rather than guessing.

Step 4: Identify the cited source that moved or exceeded its review cadence, record its previous and replacement HTTPS URLs, and document which statements depend on it. If the original source records are unavailable, do not claim that a particular source changed and do not apply a source-specific content correction.

Step 5: Validate the corrected evidence record against the authoritative specification. If validation rejects the selected class, do not publish the record. Return to the specification, select only a documented allowed value, or request a schema decision when no documented value applies.
sections.callout: The immediate correction is limited to removing PERMISSION and TIMEOUT as proposed FAILURE CLASS values. Their supported replacements and associated operational guidance remain UNKNOWN.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The correction is verifiable only when the review evidence identifies the authoritative evidence-record specification, shows the allowed FAILURE CLASS values used, and demonstrates that the corrected record passes the applicable validation. If any of that evidence is unavailable, the correction remains incomplete.

Source currency evidence must identify which prior source changed, its previous URL, its replacement HTTPS URL, the date on which the replacement was actually checked, and the statements affected by that change. Those details are currently UNKNOWN.

The JSON Schema validation specification explains that an enum restricts an instance to one of its listed values. It supports the rule against inserting absent enum values, but it does not establish the platform's actual FAILURE CLASS values or OpenAI-specific retry and permission behavior.
